title: Empirical Evaluation of a Generate–Validate–Repair Loop for Intent→Network Configuration Using a Deterministic Reachability Validator
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑archived paired experiment (cns‑m2026‑01) that measures the marginal effect of inserting a deterministic reachability validator plus at most one automated repair (a guarded GVR loop) around a single LLM generator (declared gpt‑5‑mini) for intent→device‑configuration NetOps tasks. Using a shared‑initial paired design on 300 distinct intents (600 episodes), baseline (generator candidate) execution‑validated correctness = 299/300 (99.667%); guarded pipeline = 300/300 (100.0%). Paired difference = 0.00333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Provider‑call accounting: 301 model calls (300 generator + 1 repair). All raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, per‑episode scoring JSONs, manifests, and SHA‑256 hashes are archived. We present the preregistered design, deterministic scoring semantics, full reconciliation accounting, representative artifact‑grounded examples, failure taxonomy from validator diagnostics, and operational implications grounded in archived evidence.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs promise to translate operator intent into device configurations, but unsafe or incorrect outputs can induce unintended reachability or policy changes when applied. A practical systems pattern is generate→validate→(repair): a deterministic validator gates execution and requests repairs when the generator output fails safety checks. We ask the preregistered research question (cns‑m2026‑01): Does an LLM‑driven generate–validate–repair loop (guarded) that uses a deterministic reachability validator increase the paired rate of execution‑validated correct configurations versus plain LLM generation on a curated NetOps intent→configuration corpus? Contributions (artifact‑supported): (1) a fully preregistered shared‑initial paired evaluation (study id cns‑m2026‑01; preregistration SHA‑256: 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7); (2) an archived deterministic validator and per‑episode validator traces; (3) deterministic reconciliation and provider‑call audit showing exact model‑call accounting; and (4) an evidence‑grounded failure taxonomy and operational discussion. All artifacts and SHA‑256 values cited below originate from the completed run and are archived.
sections.related_work: Empirical and prototype work has examined using LLMs for intent→config translation and verifier‑assisted generation in NetOps and adjacent domains; recent exemplars explore verifier‑gated pipelines and generate–validate–repair patterns. Our study differs by preregistering the paired shared‑initial design, freezing a single declared generator (gpt‑5‑mini) and a deterministic validator, and archiving every provider call and validator trace for deterministic reproduction. Representative nearby works (archived evidence leads) used for positioning are listed in the evidence bundle (Cited Record Ids). This study complements prior prototypes by providing a reproducible, preregistered measurement of the validator gate’s marginal effect rather than an open exploratory leaderboard comparison.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The design and analysis were preregistered (cns‑m2026‑01; preregistration SHA‑256: 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline in a shared‑initial paired design. Fixed elements: N=300 intents (stratified by deterministic complexity heuristics), shared‑initial candidate semantics (one generator proposal per intent reused by baseline and guarded conditions), repair budget ≤1 automated repair, deterministic contamination/exclusion rules, retry policy, stopping rule (process full N unless model‑call or time budgets exhausted), and statistical plan (exact McNemar two‑sided test; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples, seed=1729).Task generation and contamination. A deterministic generator produced 300 intents from public examples plus seeded synthetic templates; deterministic contamination filters excluded flagged inputs prior to selection. The final task manifest is archived: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256: 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990).Generator, validator, and repair. Declared generator: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) parses the candidate, simulates deterministic state transitions on an archived emulator snapshot, enforces task constraints (allowed_touched_fields, group constraints, preserve_unspecified_state), and returns structured pass/fail plus a validator trace. On failure, a single automated repair call (preregistered) is permitted. All model calls and validator traces were archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/scoring/ and are SHA‑256 hashed (see Disclosure).Scoring and inference. Per‑intent outcome = 1 iff the validator reports an execution‑validated configuration satisfying intent constraints and producing no unintended reachability or policy changes; else 0. Primary test: exact McNemar two‑sided on discordant pair counts (n10,n01). We report paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Reproducibility: raw outputs, per‑call provider traces, per‑episode scoring JSONs, and the reconciliation manifest are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256: 176776d1c015a652ea2d28ced2be39ffbfec9b969b72ab03e1a1193b567b6dbb; analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256: f6da505032ab388ceccda8e85084b53b8cada91a7ccc0dc65601385505f00ea6).
sections.results: Execution and reconciliation. Planned episodes = 600 (300 intents × shared initial). Completed episodes = 600; technical failures = 0. Model calls recorded = 301 total (300 generator calls + 1 repair call). Raw run results are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl — SHA‑256: 176776d1...).Primary outcomes. Aggregates (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256: 55eacb88...): baseline successes = 299/300 (0.996667); guarded successes = 300/300 (1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256: 3421adb5...): n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333333333332993. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0 (archived test implementation and seeds). Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256: 7db06f53...). Provider‑call accounting and repair. One automated repair was invoked and archived: execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json (SHA‑256: 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba). That repair converted the only baseline failure into success; validator diagnostics show no validator false negatives across the corpus. Representative episode (pair‑000001): shared initial candidate and both condition responses are identical and archived (execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256: 8f38c8be...), and corresponding per‑episode scoring JSONs are archived (execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256: 2e4a1ef1...).Artifacts for verification. Key archived artifacts and SHA‑256s cited in this manuscript (selection): execution/raw_results.jsonl (176776d1...); execution/task_manifest.jsonl (91564bb6...); execution/model_configuration.json (a40e96e2...); analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (3421adb5...); analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (f6da5050...); analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (7db06f53...); repair trace (4deb410d...). Detailed per‑episode scoring JSONs are under execution/scoring/; representative examples include execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json (635b97a3...).
sections.discussion: Interpretation. On this curated emulator corpus the generator was already near ceiling (baseline 299/300); the guarded GVR pipeline corrected the single residual error with a single additional repair call. This shows that, under high baseline generator quality and at low verification cost, a deterministic validator plus a small repair budget can eliminate occasional residual errors with minimal extra model usage. Statistical nuance. The observed discordant counts (n10=1,n01=0) are very small; the exact two‑sided McNemar implementation archived with the analysis yields p = 1.0 for the observed counts. The paired bootstrap percentile CI bounds the paired difference to ≤1% at 95% confidence (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The archived analysis code and seeds permit replication of the reported p‑value and CI (analysis artifacts are hashed and stored).Construct and external validity. The deterministic validator operationalizes safety as absence of emulator‑observed unintended reachability/policy changes in a closed snapshot; it therefore excludes production non‑determinism (firmware variability, timing, multi‑domain interactions). Shared‑initial semantics reduce within‑pair generator variance and isolate the validator effect, but do not evaluate pipelines where the guarded condition re‑queries or conditions generator context differently; both choices were preregistered and are transparent in the archives.Threats to validity. Internal: prompt sensitivity and generator nondeterminism were mitigated by the shared‑initial design and archiving raw outputs. Construct: validator = closed emulator snapshot; production dynamics are out of scope. External: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) — no multi‑model generality claim. Conclusion validity: high baseline ceiling reduces power to detect small effects; nonetheless exact counts and bootstrap CI are reported and archived.Operational implications. For NetOps deployments where generator accuracy is very high and validator latency is acceptable, a deterministic validator with a constrained repair budget can function as a low‑cost execution gate. Deployers must however assess validator fidelity on their live device fleet and consider larger repair budgets or iterative strategies where generator error rates are larger.Reproducibility and artifacts. Every artifact to reproduce the analysis is archived and SHA‑256 hashed. Representative artifact paths and SHA‑256 values are enumerated in the Disclosure Statement. The run is deterministic to the degree allowed by provider call traces and cached call entries; the full reconciliation manifest documents provider call counts and cache behavior (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256: f6da5050...).
sections.conclusion: We conducted a preregistered, artifact‑archived shared‑initial paired evaluation of a deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair (guarded GVR) against a plain LLM generator for 300 intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Observed outcomes: baseline 299/300; guarded 300/300; paired difference 0.00333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Model calls used = 301 (300 generator + 1 repair). All raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, per‑episode scoring JSONs, manifests, and SHA‑256 hashes are archived for deterministic reproduction. The guarded GVR loop eliminated the single residual failure at minimal additional model cost in this controlled emulator corpus. Broader production claims require further preregistered, artifact‑archived evaluation across diverse generator error regimes, multiple models, and live device heterogeneity.

Mandatory Disclosure Statement (artifact references and runtime facts)

Initial master prompt (immutable archive): provenance/master_prompt.txt — SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.
Preregistration: study_id = cns‑m2026‑01 — preregistration SHA‑256: 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7.
Declared generator and configuration (archived): execution/model_configuration.json — SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820. Declared model name: gpt‑5‑mini (as recorded in execution/model_configuration.json). Provider family and per‑call traces: execution/provider_calls/ (full per‑call traces archived; example shared initial trace: execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json — SHA‑256: cfd2d0956873ca732f5278c5d9bd64f0ffb008623d7fb52d2958c7769b69a791).
Orchestration framework: adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution manifest). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator v5.0) implemented for parsing, deterministic emulation, constraint checking, and structured trace output. Repair policy: one automated repair attempt permitted per intent when the validator failed (preregistered). Representative repair trace archived: execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json — SHA‑256: 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba.
Preregistered design freeze: shared‑initial paired semantics, task_count = 300, planned_episode_count = 600, maximum_model_calls = 600, repair_budget ≤1, exact McNemar two‑sided test as primary, paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) for the paired difference. The archived preregistration contains the full sampling, exclusion, retry, and analysis plans (preregistration SHA above).
Execution artifacts and hashes (selection): raw results — execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256: 176776d1c015a652ea2d28ced2be39ffbfec9b969b72ab03e1a1193b567b6dbb); task manifest — execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256: 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990); paired contingency table — analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256: 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55); reconciliation — analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA‑256: f6da505032ab388ceccda8e85084b53b8cada91a7ccc0dc65601385505f00ea6); analysis log — analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256: 7db06f53d650b2ffc5838b392740c75681480829e5db575e44a9a065eadb965e). The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 301 (300 generator + 1 repair) and completed_episode_count = 600 (planned = 600), with no technical failures (execution/execution_manifest.json).
Human role and autonomy boundary. The study was executed after the autonomy lock defined in the initial master prompt. The Research Director provided the broad topic family constraints pre‑lock (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the initial master prompt. All literature review, experiment selection, preregistration, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, peer review, and revision reported here were produced autonomously by the agentic run after the lock. No human manually edited the technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock; all manuscript content describing experiments and numbers derives from the archived autonomous artifacts cited above.
Limitations (abridged): single declared model tested; deterministic emulator validator abstracts production heterogeneity; shared‑initial semantics isolates the validator marginal effect but does not evaluate alternative pipeline requery strategies; repair budget limited to one automated attempt. Full limitations and threats to validity are discussed in the manuscript. All archived artifact paths and SHA‑256 values above are copied verbatim from the autonomous run archive and are offered as immutable references for reproducibility.
limitations: High baseline ceiling (baseline = 299/300) reduces statistical power to detect small practical effects; the run nevertheless reports exact paired counts and a paired bootstrap CI.

Construct validity: the deterministic emulator validator operationalizes safety as absence of emulator‑observed unintended reachability/policy changes in a closed snapshot; production non‑determinism (firmware variants, timing, cross‑domain interactions) is outside scope.
Model scope: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) — no claim of multi‑model generality.
Design semantics: shared‑initial paired design isolates the validator marginal effect but does not measure pipelines that requery the generator differently per condition.
Repair budget: only one automated repair attempt permitted; iterative multi‑call repair strategies were not evaluated in this confirmatory run.
